MVAPI catalog-native prediction layer

Implementation notes for spec interpretation, deviations, and follow-ups

This captures the decisions made while implementing the catalog-native Assembly101 pipeline, especially the places where real catalog behavior forced the implementation to be more specific than the original spec.

Overview

The implemented pipeline follows the spec's main contract: full catalog mount, one Assembly101 segment, direct Rerun dataloader consumption, MVAPI inference over all discovered EXO cameras, 2D and 3D COCO133 logging, immediate catalog layer registration, and Viewer screenshot validation.

The main changes are about making that contract work against the actual local Assembly101 catalog data and the prerelease Rerun dataloader behavior.

The implementation is intentionally separate from the existing full exo/ego oracle pipeline. It reuses MVAPI tracker primitives and annotation context, but all catalog mounting, schema discovery, dataloader setup, RRD writing, registration, and screenshot validation live in the new catalog-specific path.

Decisions And Deviations

Default Assembly101 segment is row 120, not row 0

Deviation

The original spec said to select sorted Assembly101 row id=0. In practice, that row exposes VideoStream:sample in the schema but returns null sample values, so it satisfies schema discovery but cannot feed the dataloader.

The default is now sorted row 120, sequence all/nusar-2021_action_both_9034-c02b_9034_user_id_2021-02-04_160111. That segment was verified to have non-null AV1 VideoStream:sample values for all eight EXO cameras.

Full catalog mount, target-only preoptimization

Deviation

The tool still mounts the full ExoEgo Forge catalog with datasets=(). It only preoptimizes ("assembly101",) by default.

The full preoptimization path started optimizing thousands of unrelated RRDs before inference could begin. Target-only preoptimization preserves full-catalog registration while keeping validation bounded to the selected Assembly101 workflow.

Assembly101 video defaults are AV1, not H.264

Decision

The initial dataloader config used h264, but catalog inspection showed VideoStream:codec as av01. The default video_codec is now av1.

A direct VideoFrameDecoder(codec="av1") probe decoded a real 3x720x1280 frame, confirming the issue was config, not invalid sample bytes.

Duration timeline adapter for Rerun dataloader

Decision

Assembly101 uses video_time: duration[ns]. The prerelease Rerun fixed-rate sample builder only treats timestamp timelines as fixed-rate eligible; duration timelines fell into the integer path and failed on Arrow/Pandas timedeltas.

The implementation adds DurationTimelineSampleIndex, which keeps the Rerun iterable dataset fetch/decode path but represents target samples as np.timedelta64[ns] while querying catalog index values as int64 nanoseconds.

Use real exo video timestamps for decoder context

Decision

Fixed-rate sample targets are not necessarily equal to real encoded-frame timestamps. The Rerun decoder needs real keyframes in its context window, so the custom sample index loads actual exo video timestamp values and uses them for context fetches.

This preserves deterministic fixed-rate target sampling while giving VideoFrameDecoder the real AV1 packets needed to decode.

Keyframe interval defaults to 300

Tradeoff

The original conservative value was 30. Assembly101 AV1 decoding needed a wider bootstrap/context window, so the default is 300.

The tradeoff is larger context queries and more decode work, but it avoids fragile early-frame failures. The sample grid also skips the bootstrap window before the first target sample.

All discovered calibrated EXO cameras are used

Decision

The tool discovers all EXO VideoStream:sample fields from the catalog schema and validates pinhole plus transform calibration for every one. There is no camera subset flag in v1.

The default validated segment exposes eight EXO cameras: C10095, C10115, C10118, C10119, C10379, C10390, C10395, and C10404.

Schema requires VideoStream but tolerates AssetVideo side data

Decision

Assembly101 video entities include both AssetVideo and VideoStream components. The implementation fails loudly only when an EXO camera has AssetVideo:blob without VideoStream:sample.

This matches the intent of "require VideoStream sample" without rejecting valid entities that carry additional asset metadata.

Catalog calibration is loaded directly from Rerun columns

Decision

The tool builds SimpleCV PinholeParameters from catalog Pinhole and Transform3D columns rather than using the SimpleCV frame loader.

Matrix values are reshaped using the catalog's column-major layout, camera conventions are inferred from Pinhole:camera_xyz, and resolution falls back to intrinsics if needed.

MVAPI behavior is reused without changing the oracle path

Decision

The implementation reuses MultiviewBodyTracker, MultiviewBodyTrackerConfig, MVHistory, and the existing annotation context helper. It does not retrofit or modify the full exo/ego oracle pipeline.

It keeps MVAPI's current upper-body filtering: shoulders and arms plus face and hands, with the rest of COCO133 masked.

Screenshot capture uses native Rerun under Xvfb

Decision

The terminal environment had no DISPLAY or Wayland socket, so fresh native Viewer windows failed. The command builder now uses xvfb-run -a rerun --new when no display is present.

This still captures from a real native Rerun Viewer session, satisfying the visual validation requirement in a headless environment.

Accept Rerun screenshot shutdown panic only after PNG exists

Tradeoff

The prerelease Viewer writes the screenshot, then exits with a panic under Xvfb while taking down the app. The capture path accepts a nonzero exit only if the expected PNG exists and has nonzero size.

This is deliberately narrow. A failed screenshot with no output file still fails the pipeline.

Screenshot layout shows a Viewer multi-view, not a tight single-camera crop

Deviation

Each per-camera screenshot file exists, but the Viewer layout rendered the 3D scene plus the EXO 2D view strip. The strip contains all EXO camera images with visible colored prediction overlays.

This meets the "each 2D view of the EXO cameras shows predictions" acceptance condition, but it is not a cropped one-camera-per-PNG presentation.

Web Viewer fallback was rejected

Tradeoff

A headless Web Viewer path was tested, but the prerelease Rerun wheel panicked because web assets were not appended to the binary. Native Viewer under Xvfb was the reliable path.

Pixi source cleanup touched unrelated package metadata

Tradeoff

Pixi resolution failed on package-local [tool.uv.sources] entries that pointed to local paths from the wrong base. Those local source declarations were moved into root Pixi features, and the per-package UV source blocks were removed from a few unrelated package pyproject.toml files.

This keeps the "Pixi only, never UV" rule coherent and makes the new catalog environments solve reproducibly.

Duplicate layer semantics should be made explicit if the API supports it

Open

The implementation relies on dataset_entry.register(..., layer_name=...) without an overwrite flag, and tests assert no duplicate override is passed. Repeated local CLI runs remount a fresh server, so they do not prove persistent duplicate behavior.

If Rerun exposes an explicit on_duplicate="error" or equivalent for layer registration, it would be better to set it directly.

Confirm whether row 120 should be the committed default

Open

Row 120 is validated and works locally, but it is a pragmatic replacement for the original row-0 default. You may want to choose a semantically preferred Assembly101 segment once you know which action/user/session should be the canonical smoke case.

Decide whether screenshots should be cropped per camera

Open

Current screenshots prove the overlays in the Viewer, but they include the full Viewer layout. A later polish step could crop each EXO panel or refine Rerun blueprints if you want one image per camera with only that camera's 2D view.

Registered Catalog Layer

Canonical viewer path

The correct artifact to inspect is the SimpleCV/Rerun catalog segment with the registered mvapi_coco133_upper_body_v1 layer enabled. This viewer is served from the same tailnet origin as the live catalog so the browser can call the catalog API directly.

Why this uses the tailnet Web Viewer

app.rerun.io was tested, but Chromium blocks a public-origin page from calling a tailnet/private-network catalog endpoint. Serving the Rerun Web Viewer and catalog proxy from pablo-dl-server.ilish-ruler.ts.net:10451 avoids that browser policy while still showing the registered catalog segment.

Open Questions

The implementation is complete against the current acceptance criteria. The remaining questions are mostly product and policy choices:

Question Why it matters
Should row 120 be the long-term default segment? It is technically valid and screenshot-validated, but may not be the domain-preferred Assembly101 action.
Should duplicate layer failure be explicit? Current behavior depends on Rerun's default registration behavior. An explicit duplicate policy would make the contract stronger.
Should screenshot artifacts be cropped per EXO camera? The current evidence shows all EXO views with overlays. Cropped per-camera captures would be easier to review at a glance.
Should keyframe interval and bootstrap window stay at 300? It is robust for the validated AV1 segment. A smaller value may work for some segments but is less safe.
